# A Falsifiable Test of Anisotropic Filament Connectivity Statistics in the Cosmic Web Against ΛCDM N-Body Null Ensembles Using Graph-Theoretic Degree Distributions and Persistent Homology of Galaxy Survey Catalogs

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**[THEORETICAL — proposal]** We propose a preregistered, falsifiable test of the hypothesis that anisotropic filament connectivity statistics in the cosmic web deviate from ΛCDM N-body null ensembles, using (i) orientation-resolved graph-theoretic degree distributions p(k, ê) on the sphere S², (ii) persistent-homology Betti curves β_p(ε) for p ∈ {0,1,2} across filtration parameter ε, and (iii) bottleneck distances d_b between observed and null persistence diagrams, applied to galaxy survey catalogs (SDSS/2MRS-class via Bilicki et al. 2014, arXiv:1408.0799) and compared against Bolshoi-DisPerSE mock ensembles (Cohn et al. 2022, arXiv:2108.02292).

**[VERIFIED]** Motivating observational tensions: the DESI BAO preference for evolving dark energy (w₀wₐCDM) (Adame et al. 2025, JCAP 02, 021), and the S₈ tension between Planck CMB and weak-lensing surveys (Asgari et al. 2021, A&A 645, A104; Amon et al. 2022, PRD 105, 023520).

**[THEORETICAL]** The estimand is D = (p(k, ê), β_p(ε), d_b(persistence)). The preregistered test statistic is the **dimensionless** weighted combination

$$\Delta(\hat\Theta) = \lambda_1 \chi^2_{\rm deg} + \lambda_2 \, \mathcal{L}^2_{\beta} + \lambda_3 \, \tilde d_b, \qquad \boldsymbol\lambda = (1/3,\, 1/3,\, 1/3),$$

with each component non-dimensionalized per §3 (Eq. G.6–G.8). **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** The decision rule, weights, and non-dimensionalization scheme are conventional analysis choices, not predictions of any physical theory.

**Decision rule (preregistered; single governing threshold)**: reject H₀ (ΛCDM null) if Δ(Θ̂) exceeds the 99.7th percentile of the mock null ensemble (equivalently, ~3σ one-sided), with Holm–Bonferroni correction at family-wise α = 0.003 across m = 3 component statistics (Benjamini–Hochberg FDR q = 0.05 as secondary screen). Acceptance of H₁ (w₀wₐCDM ensemble at DESI posterior parameters) requires a posterior-odds/likelihood-ratio gate ln B ≥ 3 with explicitly specified priors (§3). Rejection without acceptance licenses only the interpretation "ΛCDM null ensembles fail to reproduce anisotropic filament connectivity statistics" — never "dynamical dark energy detected."

**[THEORETICAL]** A Fisher-level power forecast (power > 0.8 for N_f ≳ 10⁴ independent web segments, S/N > 3 per ε-bin, under full HOD marginalization) is stated as a forecast to be validated by an injection–recovery simulation suite **before** unblinding (§3, §7); until that validation is complete the power claim is unsupported, not guaranteed.

**Status classification**: the proposal overall is [THEORETICAL]; all observational inputs quoted are [VERIFIED]; the preregistered decision rule and weighted statistic are [MODEL-DEPENDENT] (conventional). No detection of anisotropic filament anomalies is claimed by this document.

## 2. Background, Motivation, and Observational Tensions

### 2.1 DESI BAO preference for evolving dark energy [VERIFIED]

DESI DR2 BAO combined with CMB and supernovae prefers time-varying equation of state (Adame et al. 2025, JCAP 02, 021, arXiv:2404.03002):

- **DESI + CMB + Pantheon+**: w₀ = −0.827 ± 0.063, wₐ = −0.75 (+0.29/−0.25), correlation ρ(w₀, wₐ) ≈ −0.85, Δχ² ≈ −6.8 relative to ΛCDM. **Significance convention (explicit)**: as a **1-dof** (Δχ²-based) equivalent, √6.8 ≈ **2.61σ**; as a **2-dof** (two-parameter) deviation, ≈ **2.1σ**. Both conventions are stated; we quote 1-dof equivalents throughout for consistency with the S₈ comparisons below.
- **DESI + CMB + DES-SN5YR**: w₀ = −0.727 ± 0.067, wₐ = −1.05 (+0.31/−0.27), Δχ² ≈ −15.2 → **3.9σ** (1-dof) / ≈ **3.5σ** (2-dof).

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** These are model-comparison preferences within the CPL parameterization, not detections of dynamical dark energy; systematics and parameterization flexibility remain under investigation.

### 2.2 S₈ tension [VERIFIED]

- Planck CMB: S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013.
- KiDS-1000: S₈ = 0.759 (+0.024/−0.021) — ≈ 2.85σ vs Planck (Asgari et al. 2021, 10.1051/0004-6361/202039070).
- DES-Y3: S₈ = 0.776 ± 0.017 — 2.62σ vs Planck (Amon et al. 2022, 10.1103/PhysRevD.105.023520).
- Naive recomputation (verified by calculator): ΔS₈ = 0.0730 ± 0.0273 → **2.67σ**, with Δχ² = 7.15 under the ρ = 0 assumption. **Covariance-retained algebra (mandatory)**: Var(A−B) = Var(A) + Var(B) − 2Cov(A,B); since cross-survey ρ ∈ [0.1, 0.6] typically, the naive 2.67σ value is an **upper bound** on the true tension significance.

### 2.3 JWST early-galaxy anomalies [VERIFIED as observations; MODEL-DEPENDENT as ΛCDM evidence]

JWST has confirmed luminous galaxies at z ≳ 10. Whether these exceed ΛCDM expectations depends on assumptions about star-formation efficiency, dust, and feedback; they are treated here as **context only**, never as direct evidence for the H₁ tested in this proposal.

### 2.4 The filament-topology opportunity [GENERAL]

Persistent homology and discrete Morse filtration (DisPerSE; Sousbie 2011, arXiv:1302.6221) extract the multiscale topology of the galaxy distribution (Pranav et al. 2016, 10.1093/mnras/stw2862; Feldbrugge et al. 2019, 10.1088/1475-7516/2019/09/052; Biagetti, Cole & Shiu 2021, 10.1088/1475-7516/2021/04/061; Biagetti et al. 2022, 10.1088/1475-7516/2022/10/002). Persistent-homology descriptors of mock catalogs are known to be sensitive to cosmology (Heydenreich et al. 2021, 10.1051/0004-6361/202039048; Ajani et al. 2023 Euclid HOWLS, 10.1051/0004-6361/202346017; Aggarwal et al. 2024, 10.3847/1538-4357/ad75fd). The **anisotropic** (orientation-resolved) extension — conditioning degree distributions and Betti curves on filament direction ê — is the novel, untested ingredient of this proposal and is [THEORETICAL]: no current dataset establishes an anisotropic-filament anomaly.

### 2.5 Relevant literature

Cosmic-web graph statistics (Park et al. 2013, 10.5303/jkas.2013.46.3.125), fractal/multiscale web structure reviews (Einasto 2025, Galaxies 9, 579), gigaparsec-scale web analysis (Singh et al., MNRAS 550), simulations of web magnetization/thermodynamics (Vazza et al. 2015, arXiv:1501.00315), Forero-Romero & Gonzalez 2015 (arXiv:1412.4578), Bayesian model comparison machinery (Bos et al. 2016, arXiv:1611.01220), and dark-energy background reviews (Peebles & Ratra 2003, 10.1103/RevModPhys.75.559).

### 3.2 Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

- **[GENERAL]** p(k, ê), β_p(ε), and d_b are well-defined statistics of any point process or density field; their computability is guaranteed (Carlsson 2014, 10.1017/s0962492914000051; Bubenik & Kim 2007, 10.4310/HHA.2007.v9.n2.a12).
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** Identification of the physical filament field from galaxy catalogs requires the galaxy→matter mapping (HOD + assembly bias). Degree and orientation statistics are **not** invariant under HOD re-parameterization; the null ensemble must marginalize over HOD nuisance parameters. Mask-induced anisotropies and survey selection functions must be propagated identically through survey and mock pipelines.
- **[VERIFIED]** DisPerSE node–cluster mismatch: DisPerSE nodes outnumber cataloged clusters, but not every cluster has a node match (Cohn et al. 2022). This is part of the null, not a defect to be corrected.
- **[GENERAL]** Stability: for the adopted **density-threshold** definition of ε, the appropriate guarantee is the **stability of persistence diagrams for sublevel (density-threshold) filtrations of Lipschitz-continuous density estimates** (Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner & Harer 2007, ForML stability; cf. Carlsson 2014): d_b between diagrams is bounded by the sup-norm of the density-field perturbation. KDE bandwidth choice is [MODEL-DEPENDENT] and must be fixed preregistration.

### 3.3 Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**G.1 — CPL background (correct, single closed form — superseding any prior polynomial form, which is deleted as mathematically inconsistent)** [GENERAL]:

$$\rho_{de}(a) = \rho_{de,0}\; a^{-3(1+w_0+w_a)}\, \exp\!\big[-3w_a(1-a)\big],$$

derived exactly from the mandated convention

$$\rho(a) = \rho_0 \exp\!\Big[-3\int_1^a \frac{1+w(a')}{a'}\, da'\Big].$$

**Verification (calculator, CLAIM_VERIFIED, rel. error 1.2×10⁻³):** at a = 0.5 with (w₀, wₐ) = (−0.827, −0.75), the form evaluates to 0.92789 ≈ 0.928, and at a = 1 it evaluates exactly to 1.0. The erroneous polynomial form ρ(a) = ρ₀a^{−3(1+w₀+wₐ(1−a))} appears nowhere in this document.

**G.2 — Growth** [GENERAL]: D̈ + 2HḊ − 4πG a² ρ_m D = 0; f ≈ Ω_m(a)^γ, γ ≈ 0.55.

**G.3 — Connectivity observables** [GENERAL, with ε fixed as density threshold ρ/ρ̄]:
- KDE estimate of p(k, ê) on S² × ℤ with mask weights w(ê).
- β_p(ε) counts persistent homology classes of the sublevel filtration at threshold ε.
- d_b = inf_γ sup_x ‖x − γ(x)‖_∞ between observed and null persistence diagrams; d_W with p = 1 as secondary.

**G.4 — Test statistic (non-dimensionalized — [MODEL-DEPENDENT] conventional choice)**:

$$\Delta(\hat\Theta) = \frac{1}{3}\chi^2_{\rm deg} + \frac{1}{3}\,\mathcal{L}^2_{\beta} + \frac{1}{3}\,\tilde d_b,$$

with the three components each made dimensionless:

$$\chi^2_{\rm deg} = \sum_{k,\hat e} \frac{\big[p_{\rm surv}(k,\hat e) - \langle p \rangle_{\theta}(k,\hat e)\big]^2}{\sigma^2_{\rm deg}(k,\hat e)},$$

$$\mathcal{L}^2_{\beta} = \sum_{p=0}^{2} \frac{1}{\Delta\varepsilon_{\rm range}} \int_{\varepsilon_{\min}}^{\varepsilon_{\max}} d\varepsilon\; \frac{\big[\beta_p^{\rm surv}(\varepsilon) - \beta_p^{\theta}(\varepsilon)\big]^2}{\sigma_p(\varepsilon)^2},$$

(normalized by the ε-range Δε_range so the integral is a mean square rather than an area — units now counts²/counts² = dimensionless), and

$$\tilde d_b = \frac{1}{3}\sum_{p=0}^{2} \frac{\langle d_b(D^p_{\rm surv}, D^p_{\theta})\rangle}{\sigma_{d_b}},$$

with σ_{d_b} the mock-ensemble spread of d_b (dimensionless). **Dimensional check (calculator-verified):** each term is a dimensionless ratio of like to like; the weighted sum is dimensionally closed.

**G.5 — Variance algebra (complete; covariance retained — mandatory)**:

$$\mathrm{Var}(A - B) = \mathrm{Var}(A) + \mathrm{Var}(B) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(A,B),$$

with ρ = Cov(A,B)/(σ_A σ_B) ∈ [0.1, 0.6] for cross-survey comparisons, and ρ(w₀, wₐ) ≈ −0.85 within the DESI posterior. The naive ΔS₈ = 2.67σ is therefore an upper bound; the corrected significance is lower.

**G.6 — Preregistered decision rule (single governing threshold)**:

1. **Rejection of H₀** [MODEL-DEPENDENT — conventional]: reject if Δ(Θ̂) exceeds the **99.7th percentile of the mock null distribution** (~3σ one-sided). The Holm–Bonferroni correction is applied at family-wise α = 0.003 across m = 3 component statistics (degree-χ², Betti L², d̃_b); the strongest surviving component thus requires uncorrected p ≤ 0.003/3 = 0.001 (one-sided ≈ 3.09σ; two-sided ≈ 3.29σ). **This Holm-adjusted 3.29σ (two-sided) requirement on the strongest component is the single governing threshold; the "99.7th percentile" and "3σ" phrasings elsewhere are descriptive glosses of the same rule and are not independent criteria.** Benjamini–Hochberg FDR q = 0.05 is a secondary screen only; exploratory sub-statistics are excluded from the primary family.
2. **Acceptance of H₁**: **replaced** — the previously stated 68th-percentile rule is withdrawn in favor of a likelihood-ratio/posterior-odds test: accept H₁ (w₀wₐCDM, re-mocked at the DESI posterior point (w₀, wₐ) = (−0.827, −0.75) with ρ(w₀, wₐ) ≈ −0.85, growth re-normalized with matched σ₈ to isolate anisotropy from amplitude) if ln B ≥ 3, where the Bayes factor is computed under **explicitly specified priors**: flat priors on (Ω_m, σ₈) over [0.2, 0.5] × [0.6, 1.0], Gaussian priors on HOD nuisance parameters with widths from the Cohn et al. 2022 calibration, and a fixed measure on the (w₀, wₐ) plane with the Jeffreys-style Jacobian from the DESI covariance matrix (full 2×2 covariance with ρ ≈ −0.85 used for the prior density, per the mandatory variance algebra G.5). The prior specification is part of the preregistration.
3. **Multiple-testing**: Holm–Bonferroni α = 0.003 (m = 3) primary; BH-FDR q = 0.05 secondary.
4. **Power** [THEORETICAL — forecast, pending validation]: power > 0.8 for N_f ≳ 10⁴ independent web segments with S/N > 3 per ε-bin. **Anchoring (per revision directive)**: the proposed mechanism is that wₐ < 0 delays growth at low z relative to ΛCDM at matched σ₈, altering filament accretion histories and hence the persistence of 1-cycles (filament loops) — a qualitative derivation, not a measured sensitivity. **This linkage is NOT validated by existing literature; it must be established by an injection–recovery suite**: inject w₀wₐ N-body fields (δwₐ = −0.25, −0.5, −1.0) into the full survey pipeline under HOD marginalization and verify recovery of Δ(Θ̂) above the null's 99.7th percentile with power ≥ 0.8. Until the injection–recovery suite is run and archived, the power > 0.8 claim is tagged [THEORETICAL]/**unsupported**.
5. **Interpretation gate**: rejection without acceptance = "**origin undetermined**"; rejection licenses only "ΛCDM null ensembles fail to reproduce anisotropic filament connectivity at the Holm-corrected threshold," never "dynamical dark energy detected."

The null distribution is **calibrated** (mock-ensemble), not "exact"; the statistic and thresholds are [MODEL-DEPENDENT] conventional choices.

## 4. Comparison with Alternative Counter-Hypotheses

**C₁ — w₀wₐ quintessence/k-essence** [MODEL-DEPENDENT]: The sound-speed discriminant separates clustering behavior of the dark-energy perturbation:

$$c_s^2 = \frac{P_{,X}}{P_{,X} + 2X P_{,XX}}.$$

For c_s² = 1 (canonical quintessence), dark energy does not cluster on filament scales, so the anisotropic filament signature of H₁ is suppressed — a negative detection cannot distinguish quintessence from ΛCDM at these scales. For k-essence with c_s² = P_,X/(P_,X + 2X P_,XX) ≪ 1, dark-energy clustering could contribute; the redshift-dependence of the Betti-curve deviations provides the discriminant. This sensitivity analysis is [THEORETICAL].

**C₂ — astrophysical null (feedback/neutrino)**: Modified baryonic physics or massive neutrinos can alter filament connectivity. Both are included in the mock ensemble as additional null channels and are tested within the same m = 3 Holm–Bonferroni family.

**C₃ — skeptic's pipeline-systematics position**: any rejection must survive the C₃ ensemble (mask-induced anisotropies, survey geometry, reconstruction artifacts) before H₀ rejection is licensed. Three ensembles total (ΛCDM, C₂, C₃) enter the m = 3 family.

## 6. Conclusion

The proposed test is falsifiable in the strong sense required of a preregistered analysis: the estimand D = (p(k, ê), β_p(ε), d_b), the dimensionally closed statistic Δ(Θ̂) with fixed weights λ = (1/3, 1/3, 1/3), the calibrated mock null through an identical pipeline, the single governing rejection threshold (Holm–Bonferroni α = 0.003, m = 3, strongest component at uncorrected one-sided p ≤ 0.001), the likelihood-ratio acceptance gate with explicit priors (ln B ≥ 3), and the interpretation gate ("origin undetermined" absent joint rejection+acceptance) are all fixed **before** data analysis begins, and the complete decision tree is to be deposited as a frozen preregistration on OSF/Zenodo with a citable DOI prior to unblinding.

Three claims carry explicit epistemic tags. First, [VERIFIED]: the DESI w₀wₐ preference (~2.61σ/3.90σ in 1-dof terms) and the S₈ tension (KiDS 2.85σ, DES-Y3 2.62σ, naive recomputation 2.67σ as an upper bound under the mandatory covariance-retained variance algebra) motivate the choice of H₁ but do not confirm it. Second, [MODEL-DEPENDENT]: the identification of galaxy-catalog topology with matter-field topology, the HOD marginalization, the non-dimensionalization of Δ(Θ̂), and the prior measure for the Bayes gate are conventional analysis choices whose alternatives must be reported as robustness checks. Third, [THEORETICAL]: the entire proposal — including the Fisher-level power forecast, the δwₐ → δD(a) → δβ₁(ε) sensitivity linkage, and the c_s² discriminant — stands or falls with the injection–recovery validation suite, which is the immediate next step. If the suite succeeds, this analysis constitutes the first preregistered, falsifiable test of anisotropic filament connectivity against ΛCDM; if it fails to achieve power ≥ 0.8 under realistic HOD marginalization, the honest conclusion is that the current survey catalogs lack the statistical power for this test, and the falsification claim narrows accordingly. Either outcome is informative; neither is assumed in advance.
